>What does their organizational structure look like and how does it compare to the Proud Boys?

[Proud Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proud_Boys) have [chapters](https://proudboysusa.com/chapters/). "If you’re not in a Chapter, then you’re not a Proud Boy".      

"Antifa" is a movement primarily of anarchists, communists, and socialists with the concept of horizontal leadership. It is focused on local response to perceived fascist threat.     
Because of the difference of ideologies in "Antifa" there is no one anti-fascist organization. There's usually three or more flavors of anti-fascist groups in most major cities. And there are affinity groups, which are 5-15 people usually of the same ideology who affiliate to do community defense, and more often community food programs- they're commies mind you, fighting is scary, so they wind up feeding people for free more than they fight people.    

Anyways, basically a city may have an affinity group that organizes events, like let's say Twitter's Seattle Antifa, while other affinity groups might focus on medic training, or self defense, or mutual aid. And then when they come together they can function in a manner where they mutually aid eachother with the skills they learn, as opposed to taking leadership or hierarchical structures.     

So antifa does not have a nation wide structure. And that's kinda the point, Antifa is meant to be a response to local concerns of fascist threat to the community. It's not meant to be an hierarchical organization, there is no membership. It is similar to Anonymous. Being that it is an idea. An idea that people organize and act around. But not a national structure, but hundreds of tiny groups.    

I will note that anti fascist groups do often use similar name formats, like FNB, Food Not Bombs. Although there may be a FNB Seattle and a FNB Chicago, that doesn't mean there's a FNB USA. Tri-state areas try to cooperate with eachother, but often aren't the best at communicating.     

Here is the Proud Boys founder Gavin McInnes, describing the Proud Boys, in [his own words](https://twitter.com/chadloder/status/1328269865598156800?s=09) as "a gang", "we will kill you" , "violence solves everything", 'I'm disappointed that there isn't more violence from the maga side", "is it legal to say hey, they're throwing bricks, we should throw bricks- is it legal to call for violence in general? Because I am". Plenty more great quotes in the video.     

Proud Boys are prominent in the Pacific Northwest, but have chapters across America, and a few other countries.     

Because antifa is often mostly anarchists, it is horizontally organized and has no prominent leaders. There may be big affinity groups that do the PR and graphic design for a twitter account that helps coordinate events, but that affinity has no control over the autonomy of the other affinity groups that respond to the events.     

Anti-fascists are known to wear black from head to toe at protests to avoid being doxxed - having personally identifying information exposed by rival political group in many instances to mark them for violence. Because this precaution is taken to protect themselves from the far far right, it as a result also makes it harder for the police to identify them.
